transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

For months I’ve felt unusually ‘up’ and on edge all the time, like my mood is cranked way higher than normal and I can’t dial it back. It honestly feels like someone wired me to a constant high voltage and I just can't find the switch to turn it down.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt the exact opposite, such as feeling very down, sad, empty, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
No, I really haven't had periods where I felt down or lost interest in things. It's actually been the exact opposite—I've just been feeling incredibly wired and on edge for months now.
During these months of feeling 'up' and wired, have you noticed a decreased need for sleep—like feeling fully rested and energized after only a few hours of sleep?

Yes, exactly. Most nights I only get two or three hours of sleep, but I wake up completely buzzing with ideas and pacing around at 3 a.m. I don't feel tired at all, just frustrated that my physical body can't keep up with how fast my mind is racing.
Is this the very first time in your life you've experienced a period of feeling this 'up' and wired, or have you had similar episodes like this in the past?
I'm not really sure, but I've definitely never had an episode quite like this before. It has never been this intense or disruptive for me in the past.
You mentioned it has never been this intense in the past. Did you have milder periods in the past where you felt unusually energetic, active, or needed less sleep for at least a few days?
I really don't recall having any periods like this in the past, even milder ones. This level of intense energy and lack of sleep feels entirely new and different for me.

Sometimes these high-energy periods don't feel 'up' but instead show up as being extremely irritable, angry, or doing risky things out of character. Have you ever had a period in your past like that, even if it was brief?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that in the past at all. This current period over the last seven months is really the first time I've ever felt this way. Before all of this started, my mood and behavior were always very stable.

Are you currently taking any prescription medications, using recreational drugs, or do you have any physical health conditions, such as thyroid issues, that started around the same time as these symptoms?
No, I'm not taking any prescription medications and I don't use any recreational drugs. I also don't have any known physical health conditions, and as far as I know, my thyroid is perfectly fine.
How has this constant high energy and lack of sleep affected your daily life, such as your work, relationships, or how you manage your finances?

It's completely derailed my life; my lab is in absolute chaos with missed deadlines and student complaints, and my department chair warned me my job is at risk. At home, my partner is exhausted and says I’m impossible to be around right now. I haven't noticed any major financial issues, but the strain on my work and relationship is severe.
During this high-energy period, have you experienced anything unusual, like hearing voices or seeing things others don't, or feeling like you have special powers or a unique mission?

No, I haven't heard voices or seen things that aren't there. But I have felt absolutely convinced that I'm operating on a completely different level than my colleagues, uniquely capable of making a major, field-changing breakthrough that everyone else is missing.
Do you believe you have been given superhuman abilities, or do you feel you are receiving special signs, messages, or guidance from external sources to help you make this breakthrough?

No, I don't believe I have superhuman abilities or that I'm receiving any external signs or messages. It just feels like my own brain is working at an incredibly fast pace, allowing me to make these scientific connections much faster than anyone else.
Since you feel you are close to making this major breakthrough, have you felt suspicious of your colleagues, perhaps worrying that they are trying to steal your ideas or actively working against you?

No, I don't feel suspicious of them or worry that they are trying to steal my ideas. I don't think they are working against me at all; I just feel incredibly frustrated because they can't seem to keep up with my level of thinking right now.
Have you ever felt like you can read other people's thoughts, or that others can read your mind or control your actions in some way?

No, I’ve never felt like I can read minds, nor do I think anyone else can read mine or control my actions. It’s really just that my own thoughts are racing incredibly fast and my energy is so high that it’s hard to keep up with.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time manic episode characterized by an abnormally elevated and 'wired' mood, a significantly decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, and grandiosity, persisting for seven months. The symptoms have caused severe impairment in occupational and relationship functioning (lab in chaos, job at risk, severe strain on partner). There are no psychotic symptoms, and the patient has no prior history of depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes, which supports a diagnosis of a single manic episode without psychotic symptoms (F30.1).
